patches.reason: Chunks in the reserved vessel region must generate empty (no terrain, structures, features or mobs) with the void biome, so plots start clean and never get weather.
Players who were sent a vessel's plot chunks must receive block, block-entity and light updates of those chunks although they are far outside the player's view.
Every block change must reach Slipway so vessel collision shapes, mass, bounds and client meshes, and terrain bodies near vessels, are rebuilt.
Entities collide with vessel blocks in the vessel's frame, stand and walk on decks at any angle, slide off steep ones, and are carried by the moving vessel.
All block reach checks (use, break, containers, menus, signs) must measure the distance to where a vessel block is in the world, not to its plot position.
Blocks placed on a rotated vessel are oriented by the player's facing in the vessel's frame.
Look-axis placement (logs, pistons, observers) on a rotated vessel follows the player's view in the vessel's frame.

patches.feature: drops, sounds and effects on vessels
patches.reason: Entities spawned by vessel blocks (drops, experience, falling blocks) and sounds and level events at vessel blocks must appear where the vessel is, not in its far-away plot.
A player standing on a vessel has no world blocks around them; without this the server kicks them for flying after four seconds and logs and resends the air below them every ten seconds.

Vessel plot chunks are far outside the client's view-sized chunk storage; they are kept in a separate map so the client level has their blocks, block entities and light while terrain renderers never see them.
The crosshair must pick vessel blocks, in vessel space, so placing, breaking and using them works at any orientation.

Sounds the client plays itself for its own actions at vessel blocks must play where the block is; when light data for a plot section arrives, the vessel mesh must be rebuilt (the terrain renderer that would be told never sees plot sections).
Vessel blocks are outlined only when vanilla would outline a block (not with the HUD hidden, not where adventure mode forbids it, not when outlines are turned off), so they behave like world blocks.

hooks.access: reflection, guarded: absent or changed fields are skipped
hooks.reason: Iris 1.11.6 never clears this map; its shader programs hold custom uniforms that capture the ClientLevel of the world they were built for, so every world opened with a shader pack stays in memory. It is cleared when no world is loaded (Iris rebuilds entries on demand). See DESIGN.md, world-retention RCA.
